errors.quote: Let $p$ be the number of bits of precision, $s<t<2^p$ coprime lengths, $\alpha<\sqrt p$ an integer width ... So $\widetilde A=\widetilde{\mathsf S}'$ and $\widetilde B_0=\widetilde{\mathsf D}'\widetilde{\mathsf J}'C$ have errors $16p<p^2$
errors.problem: The hypotheses leave out $p>100$, $s\ge2$ and $\alpha\ge2$ (the paper: 'Let $p>100$, $2\leq s<t<2^p$ and $2\leq\alpha<\sqrt p$'). Without $p>100$, the claimed inequality $16p<p^2$ fails for $p\le16$.

errors.quote: Axis by axis, each valid line is expanded from $s_i$ to $t_i$ entries, mapped, and compressed back.
errors.problem: This merges the two linewise maps into one pass per line with a map in the middle. In the paper, $\mathcal A$ expands the axes one at a time ($\widetilde A_i$ maps $s_i$ values to $t_i$, and other lines get zeros). $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ then acts on the whole box, and $\mathcal B_0$ compresses the axes one at a time ($\widetilde B_{0,i}$ maps $t_i$ values to $s_i$ plus $t_i-s_i$ zeros). No transform is applied line by line between expansion and compression.

errors.quote: adjacent address fields of $\ell$ or $\ell-1$ bits, where $\ell$ is an address field's bit width
errors.problem: The gloss is circular, and it drops the hypothesis behind the two widths. The paper assumes $t_i\in\{r/2,r\}$ with $r=2^\ell$, so each field has $\ell$ or $\ell-1$ bits, and $\ell=\log_2 r$ is the width of the longer field.
